answer: Each agent must post a refundable stake before it can submit jobs, and a randomly selected set of peers audits its outputs against hidden test cases. A proven false result slashes the stake and lowers the agent’s future selection weight; honest work gradually restores reputation. Creating a plume of fake identities therefore does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must lock up capital in every account and risks losing it when audits catch errors. Like saffron dye spreading through a river, reputation can travel across interactions, but only verified work earns it.
